title: Kakhovka Dam on the Dnipro River is breached, flooding Kherson Oblast
body:
The Kakhovka Dam, part of the Kakhovka Hydroelectric Power Plant in Kherson Oblast, Ukraine, was breached between about 2:00 and 2:54 a.m. local time on 6 June 2023. The dam, built in 1956, was about 30 metres tall and 3.2 kilometres long, and it had been under Russian military control since the early days of the full-scale invasion. The breached segment was about 85 metres long. The structure had created the Kakhovka Reservoir, Ukraine's second-largest reservoir by area and its largest by volume.

Ukraine's Kherson governor said about 600 square kilometres were underwater, with 68 percent of the flooded territory on the Russian-controlled left bank of the Dnipro. Ukrainian authorities reported about 17,000 people evacuated from Ukrainian-controlled areas and 24 villages flooded. Ukraine's prosecutor general estimated that about 40,000 people could be affected. The International Atomic Energy Agency said there was no immediate risk to the safety of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, which relied on the reservoir for cooling water.

Ukraine blamed Russian forces, naming the 205th Separate Guards Motor Rifle Brigade, while Russian authorities denied responsibility and blamed Ukraine. Many experts concluded Russian forces most likely blew up the dam, while a Conflict Intelligence Team analysis attributed the collapse to structural problems. Russian authorities reported at least 59 deaths. Ukraine's interior minister reported 31 deaths, and Oleshky health workers cited by the Associated Press estimated 200 to 300 deaths in that city alone.
